chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazi' who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to Sa'd al-Khayr: In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Having said that,

your letter came to me in which you mentioned the necessity of knowing what must not be abandoned, and of obeying the one whose pleasure is the pleasure of Allah. And then you said to yourself what would have mortgaged your soul had you abandoned it. You marvel that the pleasure of Allah, obedience to Him, and His sincere counsel are neither accepted, nor found, nor recognized except among servants who are strangers and alone from the people — people have taken them as objects of ridicule for the evil acts they attribute to them. And it was said: A believer cannot be a true believer until he becomes more hated by the people than the carcass of a donkey.

And had it not been that you suffer from the affliction similar to what we have suffered — so that you make the strife of the people like the punishment of Allah — I seek refuge with Allah for you and for us from that — you would have drawn near despite the distance of your station.

And know, may Allah have mercy upon you, that the love of Allah cannot be attained except through the hatred of many people, nor His wilayah except through enmity with them. And losing their friendship is a small and easy matter for the attainment of that from Allah — for a people who know.

O my brother, verily Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has placed among the successors of every prophet remnants from the people of knowledge who call those who have gone astray toward guidance, and endure along with them the harm; they answer the call of Allah and call toward Allah.

So look to them — may Allah have mercy upon you — for they are in a lofty station even if they suffer lowliness in the world. They revive the dead through the Book of Allah and give sight to the blind through the light of Allah. How many slain by Iblis have they revived, and how many lost and strayed ones have they guided! They sacrifice their blood to protect the servants from destruction. How excellent is their effect upon the servants, and how ugly the effect of the servants upon them.

key_terms.بَقَايَا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ: Remnants of the people of knowledge — the spiritual heirs of the prophets who preserve and transmit divine guidance
key_terms.سِخْرِيّ: Mockery, ridicule — the social rejection experienced by those who adhere to the path of the Imams
key_terms.غُرَبَاء: Strangers (al-ghuraba') — a classical epithet for the faithful who feel alien in their own society due to their commitment to truth
key_terms.مَحَبَّةُ اللَّهِ: The love of Allah — the highest spiritual station, attainable only through detachment from worldly approval
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Wilayah — the authority, love, and guardianship of the Imam and of God; a central theological concept in Shia Islam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir write to Sa'd al-Khayr about bearing the hatred of society for God's sake?
ai.summary: In this letter from Imam al-Baqir (AS) to his trusted companion Sa'd al-Khayr, the Imam acknowledges Sa'd's letter about the difficulty of following truth in a hostile society. The Imam confirms a profound truth: the love of Allah and His wilayah can only be attained by enduring the hatred and enmity of the masses. He then describes the noble role of scholars and spiritual heirs of the prophets who, despite worldly humiliation, guide the lost, revive the spiritually dead through the Book of Allah, and sacrifice themselves for the salvation of the people.
